note: The FULL format bank — every format on every channel, as data. This is the master; formats.json stays the copy machine's write-list (social only) and its rows mirror entries here. Each row's `provenance` says where the spec came from: 'proven' = running in a machine today, 'evidenced' = derived from corpus evidence, 'drafted' = first-principles draft awaiting refinement against the corpus. Refining a drafted spec is the standing work — edit the row, the map redraws.

formats.name: Primary text / caption
formats.what: The words above the creative in the feed.
formats.form: Real sentences. First line stands alone, then short paragraphs, one idea each, blank line between.
formats.opens_with: a line that works with the creative not yet seen
formats.reads_as: something a person typed, not something a brand approved
formats.provenance: proven — copy machine `caption` row; 216 swiped examples in corpus

formats.name: Headline
formats.what: The bolded line under the creative — the ad's one claim.
formats.form: One line. A claim, a contrast, or a named enemy. Title case or sentence case, never all caps.
formats.opens_with: the noun or the tension — never the brand name
formats.reads_as: the thing you'd repeat to a friend verbatim
formats.provenance: evidenced — 15 real AdPlexity titles in corpus ('Collagen creams can't absorb. This serum can.')

formats.name: Description
formats.what: The small line under the headline. Most people never read it.
formats.form: A fragment. Reassurance or mechanism, compressed.
formats.provenance: proven — copy machine defaults (2 at 3 words)

formats.name: Angle
formats.what: The copy block's framing — the bet a brand makes, carried by many creatives. Not an ad; the idea ads are cut from.
formats.form: One framing statement a stranger could brief ten creatives from.
formats.opens_with: the belief being installed or reversed
formats.requires: a heat signal before imitation — live creatives and variant count, per METHOD.md
formats.provenance: evidenced — 223 swiped angles across four brands, ranked by heat
formats.misfiled: not a copy format — an ANGLE is a CLAIM, the second axis of the model, and it lives in brands/<brand>/strategy/angles.json. Filed here it makes a claim look like a slot. Damon's ruling 2026-09-11; left in place rather than deleted so nothing reading this bank breaks, and marked so nothing reads it as a surface.

formats.name: Static / video overlay
formats.what: Words ON the creative — the message that survives sound-off.
formats.form: Cards or captions burned into frame. Each card one beat. The set tells the whole story without audio.
formats.opens_with: the scroll-stopper — shown and said at once
formats.reads_as: what the video is saying, not a summary of it
formats.provenance: evidenced — 46 overlay sets extracted from teardowns; music-only sources carry the whole script this way

formats.name: Video ad script
formats.what: The spoken words of the ad, beat by beat.
formats.form: Beats against the source's structure — hook, problem, mechanism, proof, close. Written to be spoken, not read.
formats.opens_with: the source's own opening move, injected with our language
formats.carries_offer: in the close, exactly as the offer file words it
formats.reads_as: a person talking, whose sentences you could interrupt
formats.requires: a teardown record — scripts are rebuilt from structure, never freestyled
formats.provenance: proven — the video-teardown chain end to end (hooks v11, close v6)

formats.name: Creator caption
formats.what: The post's own words under an organic video or image.
formats.form: The creator's register exactly — fragments allowed, emoji where they'd use them, hashtags only if they would.
formats.opens_with: the line that makes the video make sense
formats.reads_as: the person who filmed it, typing on their phone
formats.requires: the creator's own voice evidence — captions are theirs, not the brand's
formats.provenance: evidenced — 360 real captions in corpus with views/likes signals

formats.name: Hook line / overlay
formats.what: The first-frame words — the two-second stop decision.
formats.form: One line on frame one. A moment shown, not a category claimed.
formats.opens_with: the formation the material calls for — free, but sourced from real language
formats.reads_as: how a person starts a sentence, never how an ad does
formats.requires: a verbatim seam — every hook traces to a real row or it gets cut
formats.provenance: proven — video-teardown 4b (entry test, four-word test, photograph test)

formats.name: Organic post (short / long)
formats.what: A story post with no offer — short-form and long-form per the machine's rows.
formats.form: Short: a few hard sentences. Long: full prose that earns its middle.
formats.opens_with: short: the sharpest line. long: a promise the length will be worth it
formats.carries_offer: never on organic; late and soft when repurposed paid
formats.reads_as: a post someone wrote because they wanted to
formats.provenance: proven — copy machine short-form + long-form rows

formats.name: Organic video script
formats.what: Spoken words for a native post — the ORGANIC lane's rebuild.
formats.form: The source's own structure held until the product must enter; commercial structure built, never inherited.
formats.opens_with: whatever the source's first two seconds did to stop someone
formats.carries_offer: one aside at most — the lane dies if it sells
formats.reads_as: the creator's own post, with our subject swapped in
formats.requires: a teardown record with lane ORGANIC
formats.provenance: proven — video-teardown ORGANIC lane (expansion stage gated in)

formats.name: Campaign email
formats.what: A one-off send to a segment.
formats.form: One idea per send. Image-built or text-built per the brand's pattern; the copy carries even inside image alts.
formats.opens_with: a first line that pays off the subject within one scroll
formats.carries_offer: usually — but the treatment (story/proof/offer) is the concept brief's call
formats.reads_as: written to one person who already let us in
formats.requires: a concept brief and a segment — the email machine's contract
formats.provenance: proven — email machine; 309 shipped <brand> sends classified in corpus

formats.name: Flow email
formats.what: A triggered send — welcome, abandon, post-purchase, winback.
formats.form: Same craft as campaign, but the trigger IS the context — never re-explain what the trigger already proves.
formats.opens_with: the moment that fired it, acknowledged in one line
formats.carries_offer: per flow position — never in the first welcome
formats.reads_as: a reply to something the reader just did
formats.provenance: drafted — flow sends sit inside the <brand> scrape, not yet split out

formats.name: Subject + preview
formats.what: The open decision — two fragments doing one job.
formats.form: Subject stops the scan; preview completes or twists it. Never restate one in the other.
formats.opens_with: curiosity or named value — never the brand name
formats.carries_offer: only when the offer IS the news
formats.reads_as: a text from someone you know
formats.provenance: evidenced — 309 subject+preview pairs indexed in the send catalogue

formats.name: Landing page / advertorial
formats.what: The click's destination — attention is spent, conviction is the job.
formats.form: Sections in an argument order: promise → problem owned → mechanism → proof → offer → objections → close. Ad-to-page scent held from the first headline.
formats.opens_with: the ad's promise, restated bigger — never a cold brand header
formats.carries_offer: yes, staged — price appears after the mechanism, never before
formats.reads_as: an editorial that happens to end in a decision
formats.requires: the angle that sent the click — page and ad are one argument
formats.provenance: evidenced — 47 swiped pages captured (incl. a 21,490px advertorial), 4 of ours

formats.name: Quiz
formats.what: Question-led conviction — the reader tells us the argument to make.
formats.form: Questions a person answers about themselves, each narrowing the recommendation; result page personalizes the pitch.
formats.opens_with: a question about THEM, not about the product
formats.provenance: proven — quiz-funnel skill + 1 shipped <brand> quiz; <competitor> runs quiz.<competitor>.com as its whole front door

formats.name: PDP
formats.what: The product's own page — where every funnel eventually lands.
formats.form: Name, one-line promise, benefit bullets in the customer's words, mechanism, ritual, guarantee exactly as the offer file words it.
formats.opens_with: the dominant problem word the avatar actually uses
formats.carries_offer: yes — the canonical price, never a channel-specific one
formats.reads_as: the calm, complete answer after the ad's excitement
formats.provenance: drafted — brand product files exist; no PDP spec has been exercised by a machine yet

scope: Copy SURFACES only — WHERE the words go: the headline, the description, the hook line, the subject line. One asset uses several at once. This is NOT the style bank (HOW the copy is written — short-form, long-form story, social proof), which is formats.json in this folder and a different axis entirely. Every ad has a surface AND a style; they are not rivals. The model: components/naming/MODEL.md
